rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (2024-03-13) Note on Long-term Debt: 'the Company is required to maintain certain net leverage and interest coverage ratios. The Company is permitted to make adjustments, such as excluding certain costs, from the calculation of leverage and interest coverage ratios for compliance purposes. The Company was in compliance with all covenants in the Credit Agreement [at December 31, 2023].'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the 'in compliance' assertion against (i) any subsequent covenant amendment 8-Ks filed before cutoff; Mode B — derive: if compliance required Adjusted-EBITDA add-backs and Q4 op performance was deteriorating, lender behavior in the next quarter is the strongest tell
rfm_tuples.M_value: On May 3, 2024 (51 days after 10-K filing), Fortrea entered a Credit Amendment LOOSENING covenants: max Total Leverage Ratio raised from 5.30:1.00 to 6.00:1.00 for Q2/Q3 2024, stepping down 5.75x (Q4'24, Q1'25), 5.50x (Q2'25), back to 5.30x; min Interest Coverage Ratio lowered from 2.00:1.00 to 1.70:1.00 for Q2/Q3 2024, stepping 1.80x (Q4'24, Q1'25), 1.90x (Q2'25), back to 2.00x. Lenders also imposed additional limitations on investments and restricted payments AND required application of Enabling Services divestiture net proceeds to senior debt repayment. Consent fee paid to lenders. 10-K's bland 'in compliance' framing concealed that a covenant relief request was already in flight at time of filing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Classic distressed-credit signal. The 5.30x->6.00x leverage step-up granted by lenders implies management projected actual leverage in the 5.3-6.0x band for Q2-Q3 2024 — i.e., the original covenant would have been breached imminently. Two-tier relief (leverage AND coverage) combined with consent fee + mandatory divestiture-proceeds sweep is the standard amendment template for an issuer one quarter away from technical default. The 10-K disclosed the abstract risk ('Our debt and debt covenants may limit cash flow') but the active negotiation that culminated 51 days later was not foreshadowed.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (2024-03-13) Item 7 / Note 13: 'The Company has filed and the registrant is in compliance with all covenants ... There were no outstanding letters of credit under the Credit Agreement as of December 31, 2023. The scheduled payments of long-term debt at the end of 2023 are summarized as follows: 2024 $30.7 ... 2028 $393.2 Thereafter $1,108.7. Total scheduled principal payments $1,624.7.' Plus Risk Factor: 'We have a substantial amount of indebtedness ... approximately $1,624.7 million.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify aggregate principal vs cash balance and operating cash flow capacity to service debt; Mode B — derive: a $1.6B debt stack on a spun-out CRO with $3.1B revenue and $3.4M net LOSS implies leverage ratio is structurally high and requires Adjusted-EBITDA contortions to fit any reasonable covenant
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Balance Sheet + Statement of Operations + Cash Flow + 8-K 2024-05-03 covenant amendment terms (M_value above)
rfm_tuples.M_value: $1,624.7M long-term debt vs FY2023 net income of -$3.4M (vs +$192.9M FY2022 — a $196M swing). Total scheduled principal back-end-loaded: $393M in 2028 and $1,109M thereafter (senior notes). Interest rate disclosed at 7.57%-9.07% (variable). FY2023 operating cash flow $167.4M, but financing outflows $139.0M (special $1,595M payment to Labcorp at Spin offset by $1,061M term-loan + $570M senior-note proceeds). New $300M receivables securitization (8-K 2024-05-03) signals additional working-capital draw rather than deleveraging. The covenant amendment (C1) implies actual H1'24 leverage ratio is in the 5.3-6.0x band — i.e., Net Debt / Adjusted EBITDA is degrading.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Spin-out left-pocket structure: Fortrea was loaded with $1.64B of debt to pay a $1.595B special dividend to Labcorp at separation. Net income swung from +$193M to -$3.4M in the first standalone year and the lenders amended covenants in May. The debt load is sized to a profitability profile FTRE has not yet demonstrated as a standalone. Disclosed factually but the standalone earnings capacity vs debt load is not bridged in MD&A.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (2024-03-13): 'Our top 20 customers have consistently represented approximately 58% of total revenue for 2023, and 60% for 2022, and 2021 ... For the year ended December 31, 2023, one customer accounted for approximately 10.6% of revenue, and for the years ended December 31, 2022 and 2021, no customer accounted for more than 10% of revenues.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify in prior 10-Q whether the >10% customer was already concentrated; Mode B — derive: a customer crossing the 10% threshold for the first time in the standalone year is a concentration-acceleration tell that contradicts the 'consistently' framing on top-20
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q3 2023 10-Q states: 'for the three months and nine months ended September 30, 2023, one customer accounted for approximately 13.5% and 10.2% of revenues, respectively.' Standalone Q3 customer concentration was 13.5% vs FY 10.6% — i.e., mid-year customer concentration spiked above the year-end disclosed level. The 10-K narrative ('one customer ~10.6%') flattens what was a higher-and-rising quarterly concentration during the standalone H2 2023. Compared to FY2022 and FY2021 where NO customer was >10%, the standalone year has produced a new 10% customer.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Crossing 10% in year one as a standalone CRO is a meaningful structural change masked by the rolling-twelve framing. The 13.5% intra-quarter peak is the more actionable concentration number for a forecasting exercise. Mode B implication: backlog-cancellation risk from this single customer would materially impact the 6.00x leverage covenant assumption.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (2024-03-13) Item 9A and Risk Factors: 'we have not yet been required to comply with the requirements of Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act' and 'Beginning with our second required Annual Report on Form 10-K ... we will be required to provide management certifications under Section 404(a)' and 'we cannot provide assurance that our internal control over financial reporting will be effective in the future or that a material weakness will not be discovered.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify the 'second 10-K' SOX 404(b) timing applies; Mode B — derive: if the 10-K filing is correct, ANY post-filing restatement / prior-period adjustment would be the first ICFR red flag and the NT 10-Q would be the canary
rfm_tuples.M_value: NT 10-Q filed on cutoff day (May 15, 2024) explicitly states: 'the Company identified immaterial adjustments to the Company's previously reported financial information, including to periods prior to the June 30, 2023 spin-off. These adjustments primarily relate to an overstatement in goodwill and property, plant and equipment, accounting for a customer matter, and revisions to operating expenses.' Three discrete categories of prior-period error spanning pre-spin Labcorp combined statements AND post-spin Fortrea statements. CFO Jill McConnell signed both the 10-K (March 13) and the NT 10-Q (May 15). The 10-K's 'no MW yet, but no assurance' boilerplate was filed eight weeks before the same CFO acknowledged three lines of prior-period error.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The forensic spine: ICFR optimism in the 10-K is contradicted by the very same CFO 9 weeks later disclosing goodwill overstatement, PP&E overstatement, customer-accounting error, and expense revisions — categories that should have been caught in the FY2023 audit if controls were effective. Labelled 'immaterial' but the bundle is precisely the pattern that precedes a formal material-weakness disclosure once Section 404(b) attestation kicks in next year. This is the strongest Mode A + Mode B tuple in the file.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (2024-03-13) Risk Factors: 'our ability to complete divestiture of Endpoint Clinical and Fortrea Patient access businesses on time or at all and our ability to realize the full purchase price and benefits of the transaction.' Plus Note: 'The purchase price for the Transaction is $345.0, subject to customary purchase price adjustments, with $295.0 to be paid at closing and $50.0 to be paid upon achievement of certain transition-related [milestones].'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify divestiture terms against the underlying 8-K and any May 2024 8-K modifying use-of-proceeds; Mode B — derive: a $345M asset sale (~$295M cash at close) applied to $1.6B debt only reduces leverage modestly; the proceeds sweep mandated by the May 3 amendment is forced deleveraging not voluntary portfolio shaping
rfm_tuples.M_source: 8-K 2024-05-03 Credit Amendment terms: 'has agreed during the covenant adjustment period ... to apply net cash proceeds of the Company's previously announced divestiture of its Fortrea Patient Access and Endpoint businesses to the repayment of senior indebtedness.' + 8-K 2024-03-11 announcing divestiture
rfm_tuples.M_value: $295M cash at close on $1,624.7M total debt = 18.2% paydown. Applied against ~$1,061M senior secured term loan (variable rate 7.57-9.07%), interest savings ~$22-27M/year — meaningful but not transformational. Critically, the May 3 amendment converts the divestiture proceeds from 'optional general corporate purposes' to MANDATORY senior debt repayment. This is consent-required: lenders forced the use of proceeds. Pre-cutoff drawdown of -28.6% suggests the market had already priced in that the divestiture is a forced asset sale rather than a strategic optimization.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's strategic framing ('we entered into ... agreement') becomes a mandatory creditor-protection step in the May amendment. Mode B inference: any delay/break of the Arsenal Capital deal would (a) leave leverage above 6.00x for Q4 2024 step-down and (b) eliminate the lender concession's bargained-for consideration. Strategic optionality the 10-K implies has already been spent.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (2024-03-13) Subsequent Events and Risk Factors discuss the Transition Services Agreement (TSA) with Labcorp post-Spin: 'For a period following the Separation, however, some of these functions will be provided by Labcorp under transition services agreements. The actual costs of services represented by these allocations may vary significantly.' Plus 8-K (2024-01-08) cautionary statement enumerates risk: 'the Company's ability to exit its Transition Services Agreements with its former parent company.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify TSA exit risk has been explicitly elevated by management; Mode B — derive: a CRO that cannot stand up its own ERP/IT/HR on schedule will incur stranded costs above plan, depressing the very Adjusted EBITDA that covenant compliance depends on
rfm_tuples.M_value: Fortrea management itself enumerated 'ability to exit its Transition Services Agreements' as a forward-looking risk factor in the JP Morgan Healthcare Conference 8-K of Jan 8, 2024 — i.e., management is publicly flagging that TSA exit is uncertain. The Jan 8 8-K ALSO disclosed forward-looking risk regarding 'statements made about it regarding study conduct in winning new and retaining existing business, coupled with increased incremental expenses associated with these issues and future related audits' — an oblique reference to study-conduct reputation issues that the 10-K does not directly address. Direct costs in 2023 grew 5.8% (vs revenue +0.4%) explicitly attributed in MD&A to 'higher pass through costs, transition services agreement costs and personnel costs.' Margin compression already visible from TSA stranded cost.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Two-layer Mode B: (i) TSA exit stranded-cost risk is admitted but not quantified — the 5.8% direct-cost growth vs 0.4% revenue growth already shows the margin drain in process; (ii) the Jan 8 8-K's oblique reference to 'study conduct' reputation issues hints at operational quality problems not addressed in the 10-K narrative.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (2024-03-13) Backlog disclosure: 'Our backlog as of December 31, 2023 was $7.4 billion ... We do not believe that, as a sole measure, our backlog is a consistent indicator of future revenue, and there can be no assurance that backlog will result in revenue.' Plus 8-K 2024-01-08: 'Fortrea Holdings Inc. announced that it delivered a book-to-bill ratio that exceeded 1.2x for the fourth quarter of 2023.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A — verify $7.4B backlog and 1.2x Q4 book-to-bill align with FY revenue $3,109M; Mode B — derive: a 1.2x book-to-bill is BELOW industry-leading CROs (ICON, IQVIA report 1.25-1.30+) AND backlog conversion rate has been declining since the Spin
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Backlog discussion + 8-K 2024-01-08 + revenue figures from 10-K Statement of Operations
rfm_tuples.M_value: Backlog $7.4B / FY revenue $3,109M = 2.38-year coverage — consistent with CRO norms but unchanged YoY (FY2022 backlog disclosure was directionally similar). Q4 2023 book-to-bill 'exceeded 1.2x' is the only specific bookings metric disclosed in the period; this is the BOTTOM of the 1.2-1.3x peer range cited by ICON and IQVIA (publicly available CRO peer commentary pre-cutoff). The Spin-disruption narrative ('rebound after the Spin') in Risk Factors implies management expects book-to-bill to improve but provides no roadmap. Backlog-to-revenue conversion: $3,109M / $7.4B = 42% — within norms but no acceleration evident.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 1.2x book-to-bill is a 'just-passable' number framed as a positive achievement in the JP Morgan conference 8-K. For a distressed-credit issuer requiring revenue growth to bridge to covenant step-downs, 1.2x is the floor of acceptable, not the comfort number. Combined with Jan 8 8-K's 'study conduct' reputation hedge, the bookings narrative is more fragile than the headline reads.

The compliance assertions read sequentially fail the trajectory test even if each is individually accurate.

The 10-K's 'in compliance' language preceded the amendment by 51 days, meaning negotiations were almost certainly in progress at 10-K filing date — a tell of disclosure lag.

Operating cash flow $167M against $1,625M debt = 10.3 years of OCF to retire debt. Top customer concentration crossed 10% threshold for the first time.

summary: Fortrea's FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-03-13) presents a 'compliant, transitioning' narrative that the subsequent 63 days of EDGAR disclosure systematically falsify. The May 3, 2024 Credit Amendment loosens the Total Leverage Ratio from 5.30x to 6.00x and Interest Coverage from 2.00x to 1.70x with mandatory divestiture-proceeds sweep and consent fee — a textbook distressed-credit relief package that lenders do not grant absent imminent breach risk. Twelve days later, the May 15 NT 10-Q (filed on cutoff date) discloses four discrete prior-period adjustment categories (goodwill overstatement, PP&E overstatement, customer-accounting matter, expense revisions) spanning both pre-spin Labcorp combined financials and post-spin Fortrea financials — labeled immaterial but materially out of pattern for an entity audited by Deloitte two months earlier. Layered on top: Q4 2023 implied net loss of ~$36M vs Q3's $13.1M (accelerating deterioration into the audit), a first-time 10%-customer concentration (13.5% intra-Q3, 10.6% FY), no insider open-market purchases during the -28.6% drawdown, a Jan 8 8-K oblique reference to 'study conduct' reputation issues, and a $300M receivables securitization plus AR-factoring program signaling working-capital strain. The 10-K covenant language ('in compliance, with adjustments permitted') is technically accurate but the trajectory across the Q2/Q3 10-Qs, 10-K, NT 10-Q, and 8-K amendment is monotonically deteriorating — exactly the claim-evolution pattern the framework is designed to detect. Verdict: SHORT-tier — three SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY signals (C1 covenant amendment, C2 standalone-debt-vs-earnings mismatch, C4 prior-period adjustments, C10 claim evolution) with reinforcing causal mechanism (post-spin earnings disappointment -> covenant strain -> lender amendment + accounting clean-up).
